title: Beverage Container Return Scheme launch, costs and return points
asked: MPs asked how the Beverage Container Return Scheme will work: how return points will be known and accessible, how producers and consumers will be affected by costs, how many reverse vending machines will be ready at launch, and how deposits and unredeemed deposits will be managed. They also asked about affordability for lower-income households and assistance for vulnerable residents.
asked_by: Ms Poh Li San, Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Foo Cexiang, Ms Valerie Lee and Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
response: The Senior Minister of State said the Beverage Container Return Scheme will start on 1 April, with a fully refundable 10-cent deposit on regulated beverage containers and a producer fee of three to four cents per container. At launch there will be over 1,000 reverse vending machines, with a target to double this to 2,000 within the first year; 90% of HDB residents will be within a five-minute walk of a return point. The transition period has been extended from three to six months, and a $2,500 transition grant is available for smaller businesses. NEA will monitor beverage prices, and EZ-Link SimplyGo is available for refunds, with no cash or cash voucher refunds planned at this point.

key_points.point: The scheme will commence on 1 April this year.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: which will commence on 1 April this year

key_points.point: All regulated beverage containers will attract a fully refundable 10-cent deposit.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: All regulated beverage containers supplied in Singapore will attract a 10-cent deposit, which is fully refundable.

key_points.point: Producers will pay a producer fee of three to four cents per container to BCRS Ltd.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: All producers will also need to pay a producer fee of three to four cents per container to the scheme operator, BCRS Ltd.

key_points.point: Producers of about 80% of beverage containers can incorporate the deposit mark and barcode requirements directly on their containers.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: producers of about 80% of beverage containers can incorporate the deposit mark and barcode requirements directly on their containers.

key_points.point: The transition period has been extended from three months to six months.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: we have extended the transition period from three months, to six months.

key_points.point: A transition grant of $2,500 has been introduced to help smaller businesses.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: We also introduced a transition grant of $2,500 to help smaller businesses.

key_points.point: At launch, the public can return containers at over 1,000 Reverse Vending Machines across Singapore for a 10-cent refund.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: the public can return their empty plastic and metal beverage containers bearing the deposit mark at over 1,000 Reverse Vending Machines (RVMs) located across Singapore to obtain a 10-cent refund.

key_points.point: 90% of residents in HDB housing estates will live within a five-minute walk of a return point.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: 90% of residents in HDB housing estates will live within a five-minute walk to one of these return points.

key_points.point: The aim is to double the number of return points to 2,000 RVMs within the first year.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: We aim to double the number of return points to 2,000 RVMs within the first year of implementation.

key_points.point: The deposit mark will remain necessary because the scheme does not cover 100% of beverage containers.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: the deposit mark will be necessary for some time as the scheme does not cover 100% of beverage containers

key_points.point: EZ-Link SimplyGo is available for refunds, and cash or cash voucher refunds are not planned at this point.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: EZ-Link SimplyGo is available as a refund methodology and there will be further refund methodologies. We are not, at this point, planning for cash or cash voucher as forms of refund.

key_points.point: There is a contractual requirement for the machines to maintain 90% up-time.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: There is a contractual requirement for these machines to maintain 90% up-time.

key_points.point: The assessment is that 80% of the market will have a 3% to 4% increase.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: Our assessment is that 80% of the market will have a 3% to 4% increase.

key_points.point: For a smaller producer putting less than 50,000 containers to market per year, the $2,500 grant is more than sufficient to cover about $2,000 in first-year costs.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: For a smaller producer, which we define as less than 50,000 beverage containers put to market per year, and that represents about one quarter of the producers in our estimate, the $2,500 is more than sufficient to cover both the product registration cost as well as the producer fees for the first year, which is about $2,000 in total.

key_points.point: NEA will watch beverage prices closely after the scheme is introduced and through the transition.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: NEA will be watching the beverage prices after we introduce this scheme and through the transition, very closely.

key_points.point: If there is evidence of collusion or profiteering, there are mechanisms for that to be reported and dealt with.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: If there is evidence of collusion or profiteering, there are mechanisms for that to be reported and dealt with.

left_open: The exact locations of all reverse vending machines at launch.
How retailers and shops will be prevented from selling beverages in non-returnable containers at the same price as returnable containers.
Specific assistance for vulnerable residents not living near return points to claim their deposits.
Whether alternatives with lower cost impact on producers and consumers were considered.
How unredeemed deposits will be managed.
The specific affordability impact on lower-income households before the April 2026 launch.
The criteria that would trigger a review of the deposit value.
Assessment of the risk that the scheme eliminates the discount beverage segment.
What specific action will be taken if price increases exceed three to four cents.
What percentage price increase is considered acceptable for consumers to bear.
supplementary: Supplementary questions focused on operational capacity, consumer price protection, support for small producers, refund methods, deposit review, and recycling targets.
